request: Активнее поворачивать голову по направлению вращения; убрать выступ за ухом на кадрах 00 и 01.
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: revision of an existing ten-frame Shiba spin animation.
IMAGE 1 is the EDIT TARGET: ten chronological Kaifik dog sprites in two rows of five, currently on dark gray for inspection. IMAGE 2 is a HEAD/IDENTITY reference of the same dog turning his muzzle left; do not copy its body pose.
Keep all TEN existing bodies, paws, tails, body orientations, body scale, placements, sequence, exact art style, red/cream colors and canvas layout as close to the edit target as possible. CHANGE ONLY THE HEAD/UPPER NECK AND A SMALL EAR DEFECT. This is a targeted correction, not a new animation. Do not redesign the dog or change the stepping poses.
USER CORRECTION 1: the head must turn MUCH MORE ACTIVELY TOWARD THE DIRECTION OF THE SPIN. Currently the dog mostly looks ahead or at the viewer and the head rotates rigidly with the torso. Show deliberate head-leading movement: muzzle/nose/eyes/ears turn in yaw 30-45 degrees AHEAD of the shoulders toward the NEXT body orientation. This is horizontal head rotation into the turn, not just lifting the chin or moving the pupils. Keep natural canine neck anatomy, no backwards 180-degree head twists. Do not chase the tail. The body sequence goes rightward -> front -> leftward -> rear -> rightward, and the head must anticipate the next phase:
Frame00 upper-left: chest/body rightward, turn the whole head clearly toward viewer/front, anticipating chest coming frontal.
Frame01 top second: chest frontal, turn muzzle distinctly to SCREEN LEFT, already looking into the coming left turn. Do not keep front-facing nose.
Frame02 top third: chest slightly left, head in unmistakable LEFT PROFILE, nose projects screen LEFT of forehead and ONLY near eye is clearly visible; natural neck turn.
Frame03 top fourth: body left profile; turn head further into the left/away direction, showing more back of head and far cheek than before. Neck follows the left turn.
Frame04 top fifth: body rear-left, head points AWAY, mostly back of skull and two ear backs. No sideways upward gaze.
Frame05 bottom first: body rear-left advancing to rear; head already begins rotating from fully away toward the next RIGHTWARD side of the turn.
Frame06 bottom second: body directly rear-facing; head clearly turns toward SCREEN RIGHT and a small amount of right-facing muzzle/profile becomes visible.
Frame07 bottom third: body rear-right; head more strongly right-facing, nose leads into the rightward step.
Frame08 bottom fourth: body coming rightward; head already turns toward viewer/front in a three-quarter pose, anticipating the next turn.
Frame09 bottom fifth: body right profile; head turns further toward viewer/front, so the loop into frame00 is continuous. No sudden nose-direction reversal at loop seam.
Use smooth progressive head turns and small natural neck follow-through. Preserve the head's physical size, exact Shiba facial anatomy, ear size and markings; do not shrink/grow heads.
USER CORRECTION 2: in frames00 and01 there is an unwanted small TAN OVAL/EAR-LIKE LUMP immediately BEHIND the IMAGE-LEFT EAR. REMOVE this extra protrusion. There must be exactly TWO triangular ears per dog, clean coherent head and neck silhouette with natural fur. No third ear, extra oval flap, lump, collar, tag or object behind either ear. Preserve the real curled tail on the rump (far away from the ear); do not confuse tail with this local head defect.
Output exactly the same TWO ROWS OF FIVE complete dogs, same proportions and spacing, all paws/tails/ears visible. Background truly transparent, dog pixels opaque, clean antialiased fur edges, no dark matte halo. Remove dark inspection background. No labels, arrows, numbers, shadows, props, ghost ears or extra parts. Preserve all other artwork.
